content: Hypertension is a frequent co-morbidity in patients with diabetes, particularly type 2 diabetes. The simultaneous presence of these conditions significantly increases the risk of both renal and cardiovascular damage. Diabetes is the leading cause of end-stage renal disease in the United States. The optimal treatment for diabetic patients with hypertension includes the following: ACE inhibitors: Calcium channel blockers: These are effective in managing hypertension in this population. Low-dose diuretics: These are also recommended as part of the treatment regimen. Supporting Clinical Trial Data LIFE Study (2002) Design: A double-blinded, randomized, parallel-group trial. Participants: 1,195 patients with diabetes, hypertension, and left ventricular hypertrophy (confirmed via electrocardiograms). Interventions: Patients were treated with either losartan or atenolol. Duration: 4 years. Findings: Losartan was more effective than atenolol in reducing composite endpoints, including cardiovascular morbidity and all-cause mortality, in patients with hypertension, diabetes, and left ventricular hypertrophy. CALM Study (2000) Design: A double-blinded, prospective, randomized, parallel-group, multicenter trial conducted across 4 countries and 37 centers. Participants: 199 patients with diabetes and hypertension. Interventions: Patients were treated with candesartan, lisinopril, or a combination of both. Duration: 4-week placebo run-in period. 12 weeks of monotherapy with either candesartan or lisinopril. Followed by 12 weeks of either continued monotherapy or combination therapy. Objective: Findings: FACET Study (1998) Design: An open-label, randomized trial. Participants: 380 hypertensive diabetic patients. Interventions: Patients were treated with either fosinopril (20 mg/day) or amlodipine (10 mg/day). Duration: 3.5 years. Inclusion Criteria: Exclusion Criteria: Patients with a history of coronary heart disease or stroke, serum creatinine > 1.5 mg/dL, albuminuria > 40 micrograms/min, or those using lipid-lowering drugs, aspirin, or antihypertensive agents other than beta-blockers or diuretics. Findings: Fosinopril significantly reduced the risk of composite endpoints, including acute myocardial infarction, stroke, or hospitalization due to angina, compared to amlodipine (hazard ratio = 0.49, 95% CI = 0.26–0.95). However, there were no significant differences between the two groups in terms of total serum cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, HbA1c, fasting serum glucose, or plasma insulin levels.
